issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify lectureName as a String, and the template expects students to add a String attribute. The solution, however, declares lectureName as type LectureName (a custom wrapper), introducing a type mismatch across artifacts and deviating from the specified design.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the same type for lectureName across all artifacts. Either change the solution to declare lectureName as String (matching the problem and template) or update the problem statement and template to explicitly require and document a LectureName value object. Preferably revert the solution to String to match the exercise description and UML.

issues.description: The solution's getter and setter signatures treat lectureName as a String (getLectureName() returns String, setLectureName(String)), but the actual field is declared as LectureName. These signature/field type mismatches will cause compilation errors and confuse students about the expected types.
issues.suggestedFix: Make getter/setter signatures consistent with the field type. If lectureName remains LectureName, change getLectureName() to return LectureName and setLectureName(LectureName). If lectureName should be String (as in the problem), change the field to String and keep the current getter/setter signatures.

issues.description: The problem description and UML expect a constructor that initializes lectureName as a String (first parameter) followed by the integer attributes. The solution constructor instead expects a LectureName object as the first parameter, creating a parameter-type mismatch between the specification and the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the constructor parameter types with the exercise specification. Either change the constructor to accept a String for lectureName (matching the problem/UML) or update the problem statement and template to require a LectureName object and adjust tests/documentation accordingly. The simpler fix is to use String in the constructor.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify the lectureName attribute as a String (lectureName: String), but the solution introduces a new LectureName class and declares the field as LectureName. This creates a cross-artifact naming/type mismatch for the same conceptual entity (the lecture's name) and may confuse students who expect to work with a String-based lectureName in the template and exercises.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of the lecture name across artifacts. Either revert the solution to use a String lectureName (matching the problem statement and UML) or update the problem statement and template to document and use the LectureName class consistently. Prefer keeping lectureName as String for this introductory exercise to avoid unnecessary cognitive load.
